newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei expected to stick close to 20,000.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei expected to stick close to 20,000.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key benchmark is expected to stay close to the 20,000-point threshold on Monday, supported by blue chips, which began to revive late last week, brokers said. They said banks, which announced 1996/97 earnings on Friday, could also lend a hand.
The Nikkei 225 closed up 131.61 points, or 0.66 percent, at 20,009.00 on Friday. June futures rose 180 to 20,030.

"Wall Street was firm on Friday, so if the yen stabilises at its current level between 110 and 120, it should not provide investors with a strong reason to sell," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities.
Brokers added that bank shares could firm after nine of Japan's top 10 commercial banks said on Friday that they posted parent current profits in the past business year which ended March 31.
Only Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), currently under fire for its connection to a racketeer scandal, reported a parent current loss.
In 1995/96, seven of the 10 big banks posted losses.
"Banks' bad-loan problems seem to have cleared up quite a bit and this factor could be appreciated by the market," said a market analyst at a foreign brokerage.
